result:
I've audited `/contact-lead/` and all 58 checks are judged. The validator reports 58/58, with nothing missing, unknown, duplicated, blocked or skipped. The page is a static council contact form with no JavaScript: name, email and message fields, a "Send enquiry" button, and a box with the phone number and opening hours.

**Scorecard**

```
Overall: 86/100 (needs work)

Speed & Stability      93  good
Memory Health         100  good
Usability & UX         66  needs work
Inclusivity & Reach    95  good
Discoverability & AI   85  needs work
Trust & Resilience     76  needs work

Do these first:
  1. [critical] Make POST /enquiry work: validate server-side, store/route the enquiry, 303-redirect to a confirmation page
  2. [high] Build the success state: confirmation page with the promised reference, reply expectation and focus/role=status announcement
  3. [medium] Replace raw server error pages with branded 4xx/5xx pages; on a failed POST, re-render the form with values kept and a retry
```

The interactive report is at `reports-cpa/127_0_0_1_8765/scorecard.html`. Its History tab holds four runs on this host, but each one audits a different page (booking, account-recovery, catalogue, contact). The changes there compare different pages, not one page improving.

**Main findings**
- **Nobody can send an enquiry.** I recorded a real submission with valid details. It ends on a bare "501 Unsupported method" page with no site header and no way back to the form. The test server is a simple static file server, so production may behave differently.
- **The promised reference never appears.** The page says "we will give you a reference", but there is no confirmation page or success message anywhere.
- **The header links are wrong.** "Contact" is marked as the current page for screen readers but opens a raw list of server folders. "Inbox" leads to a "not found" page.
- **The button disappears in high-contrast mode.** It has no border, so "Send enquiry" shows as plain bold text.
- **The contact details box is cramped.** It uses a fixed-width label column, so the phone number breaks across two lines at every desktop width. At 780px wide, the opening hours wrap almost one word per line.
- **Error feedback is minimal.** Mistakes only trigger the browser's own pop-up message, and a message made of spaces is accepted.
- **Security is weak.** Personal details are sent over plain HTTP, with no security headers and no protection against forged form submissions.

Lower-priority findings:
- no dark mode
- the phone number is not tappable to call
- no privacy notice where personal data is collected
- the text size is fixed and ignores the user's setting
- the stylesheet is sent uncompressed and never cached
- no page description, canonical link, robots.txt or sitemap
- no machine-readable contact details for search engines
- no animated transitions between pages

Everything is in `reports-cpa/127_0_0_1_8765/2026-10-09T00-39-23-039Z/` (`report.json`, `report.md`, `evidence/`). I updated `latest.txt` to this run. Repointing the `latest` symlink needed approval and was declined, so it still points at the earlier catalogue run. This was report-only mode, so I changed no site source and committed nothing. The Cloudflare connector needs re-authorising in your claude.ai connector settings, but this audit didn't need it.

**TLDR:** All 58 checks judged (22 issues, 23 pass, 13 not applicable), producing 18 findings: 1 critical, 1 high, 8 medium and 8 low. Evidence came from:
- screenshots at desktop, 780px, phone, dark and high-contrast settings, plus a video of a real form submission
- my own probes of the form, links and destinations, plus a run under an Arabic locale and Tokyo time zone
- the axe accessibility scanner, the accessibility tree with a real Tab walk, and touch-target sizes
- a CSS feature check, layout, and a slowed-down mobile performance trace
- a network recording, security headers, cookies, trackers and a secrets scan
- a check of what search crawlers see, a reload with the network off, and before/after memory snapshots
- the Modern Web Guidance and Baseline lookups

The single highest-leverage fix is making `POST /enquiry` work and redirect to a confirmation page with the reference, because right now the page's only task always fails.
